title: A string with a small buffer
hints: Keep four members: a `char local[16]`, a `char* heap` (null for inline strings), the length, and the heap capacity. Every function then starts with "which buffer is the text in?": `heap ? heap : local`.

Moving cannot just steal a pointer when the text is inline, because the text is part of the other object: copy the characters instead. Write that logic once (a private "take over the other string's contents" helper) and use it for both moving and swapping.
requirements: Short strings never touch the heap; long strings use exactly one heap block at a time.
Appending grows geometrically and keeps the text and its terminating zero intact.
Copy, move, assignment and self-assignment are all correct, with no leaks and no double frees.
`c_str()` and `view()` always describe the current text.
stretch: Measure it: build 100 000 strings of 8 characters with `SmallString` and with `std::vector<char>`, and compare how many heap allocations and how much time each takes.
